Filled pauses in Italian dialogue

Source: R/data.R
disfluencies.Rd

Filled pauses (ehm, eeh) in 60 turns from each of 40 speakers in 20 Italian Map Task dialogues, in which an instruction giver guides a follower along a route. Filled pauses are rare: about 4% of turns contain one, about 0.4 per 100 syllables. Many turns are fluent and cannot contain a filled pause at all, so the data have more zeros than a Poisson model predicts. Givers produce more filled pauses than followers. For zero-inflated count models with an exposure.

Usage

disfluencies

Format

A tibble with 2400 rows and 6 columns:

dialogue

Dialogue ID, D01 to D20.

speaker

Speaker ID, S01 to S40.

role

"follower" or "giver".

turn

Turn number, 1 to 60.

syllables

Length of the turn in syllables.

filled_pauses

Number of filled pauses in the turn.

Source

data-raw/disfluencies.R

Details

True model: with probability 0.55 a turn is fluent and has no filled pauses. Otherwise the count is Poisson with mean rate * syllables / 100, where rate is 1.2 for givers and 0.6 for followers, multiplied by a speaker effect (SD 0.5 on the log scale). Turn lengths are log-normal with a median of 9 syllables.

References

Di Napoli, J. (2020). Filled pauses and prolongations in Roman Italian task-oriented dialogue. Laughter and Other Non-Verbal Vocalisations Workshop 2020. doi:10.4119/lw2020-915

Examples

table(disfluencies$filled_pauses)
#> 
#>    0    1    2    3    5 
#> 2298   82   17    2    1
